title: A lower sun, so the day rakes across the city instead of shining down it
why: Material-realism phase (2026-09-17), the last item on the founder's list: lighting that reveals materials. After the ground, ivory, roofs, gold, glass, plinths, plaster, grass and planting passes, the light was still a 52-degree midday sun: frontal on every facade, with each shadow dropped at its own foot. At 40 degrees the same sun rakes: a balustrade lays its shadow across the lawn at Lantern Lane, facades keep a lit and a shaded side, and the aerial reads with depth between buildings. Brightness is unchanged -- this turns the sun, it does not dim it.
judged: 9 identical cameras, one session, three states (52 deg; 40 deg; 40 deg with a sharper source). Evidence 2026-09-17-LT02-sun-angle.

sun.note: The source angle goes 1.2 -> 0.7 degrees so a contact shadow has an edge; the sun's own intensity (70,000 lux), colour and every fill light are untouched.
